title: Restriction of integral lattice pairs
statement: Let X be a scheme, J its pro-etale topology, R and S sheaves of commutative rings on J, a : R → S a ring-sheaf morphism, and L an S-module sheaf. An integral lattice pair on U consists of a finite locally free R|U-module P and a specified isomorphism S|U ⊗ P ≅ L|U, with the sheafified tensor product. For f : V → U and a lattice pair P on U, restriction of its integral module is finite locally free and scalar extension commutes with this restriction via the canonical sheafification-unit comparison. These give a lattice pair P|V. For every T over V, its embedded image equals the embedded image of P on the object T → V → U. [lem-weil-pbc-lattice-pair-image-classification, def-pur-localized-ringed-site, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(6), pp. 59–60; Descent and an exact presentation of lattice classes

proof.text: Construct the tensor comparison from the restricted sheafification unit. Restriction preserves local bijectivity, hence the comparison is invertible. Pull back finite free basis covers. The comparison on the unit proves the image formula.

theorem IntegralLatticePair.restrict_image
    {L : SheafOfModules.{u + 1} 𝓢} (P : IntegralLatticePair a L U)
    (T : (Over V)ᵒᵖ) :
    (P.restrict a f).image T = P.image ((Over.map f).op.obj T)
